00Summary at a Glance

Current stance: lean toward waiting · stage entries after earnings
All three companies are earning more than at any point in their history, yet the market is betting that "this is the peak of earnings." Today (Oct 13) combined heavy foreign selling with worries about Chinese competition, so the analysis favors waiting for late-October earnings and a calmer flow picture, then entering in stages rather than buying all at once.
  • The fundamentals are very strong. SK hynix posted a 76% operating margin in Q2, Samsung Electronics' preliminary Q3 operating profit was KRW 107.4 tn (about USD 80 bn, the first quarter above KRW 100 tn for any Korean company), and Micron's gross margin last quarter was 87%.
  • Share prices have fallen sharply from their highs. Versus the June peak, SK hynix is down 51%, Samsung Electronics 38% and Micron 21%. Estimated 2026 P/E ratios have dropped to 4-6x.
  • Why today was unfavorable. KOSPI fell 5.46% (foreign investors net sold KRW 4.5 tn), Samsung Electronics ended its share buyback early (Oct 6), China's CXMT announced a push into server DRAM, and the US 10-year yield sits above 5.2%.
  • Next checkpoints. TSMC earnings on Oct 15, the Bank of Korea rate decision (MPC) on Oct 22, SK hynix Q3 earnings on Oct 27-29, the FOMC on Oct 28, Samsung Electronics' final results in late October, and Micron earnings in mid-to-late December.

01Who Makes What

The three companies form a three-player oligopoly that effectively splits the global DRAM market. HBM (high-bandwidth memory), which AI servers require, is the core profit driver, and as capacity shifts toward HBM, prices for conventional DRAM and NAND have risen along with it.

The memory big threeSK hynix, Samsung Electronics and Micron make DRAM and HBM
HBM supply
AI acceleratorsNvidia (Rubin), AMD (MI450), Google TPU and others. HBM is packaged right next to the GPU
Server sales
Big Tech data centersAI capex at Microsoft, Google, Meta, OpenAI and others

Is the "AI Memory Supercycle" Real?

The numbers say yes. But memory has historically been the most cyclical corner of the semiconductor industry, and that has to be weighed alongside them.

  • What has changed: HBM consumes roughly three times as much wafer area as standard DRAM of the same capacity. The more HBM a maker produces, the less conventional DRAM it supplies, which pushes prices up.
  • Pricing power: Micron said it contracted most of its 2027 HBM volume at sharply higher prices. Nvidia has said memory costs could pull its gross margin down to 71-72%. Profit is shifting toward memory makers.
  • Easy to miss: Margins of 76-87% have no precedent in any past cycle. The market assigns only a 4-6x P/E because it doubts these profits can last two to three years.

Profits are setting a new record every quarter. Q3 consensus for SK hynix ranges from KRW 74 tn to 78 tn depending on the data provider. Micron guided next-quarter revenue to $61.5 bn with a 86.25% gross margin. The share price decline is not because profits have turned down, but because the market is pricing in the timing of that turn early, and that is the starting point of this report.

03The HBM Three-Way Race: Who Takes How Much

HBM is the core of all three companies' profits, but the split is not fixed. The leader's share is slipping while the No. 2 player closes in quickly.

ItemSK hynixSamsung ElectronicsMicronInterpretation
HBM revenue share (Q2 2025)64%——Near-monopoly a year ago
HBM revenue share (Q2 2026)50%33%about 17%From monopoly to oligopoly competition
2026 HBM4 share forecast54-55%28-29%17-18%Forecast based on combined Nvidia, Google and AMD demand
Share of Nvidia volume72% → 63%Expected to rise—Daishin Securities' 2025 → 2026 forecast. JP Morgan raises Samsung's share from 25% to 35%
Latest quarterly operating margin76.3%about 55% (company-wide)81.6%Samsung looks lower because foundry and appliances are blended in

Profit can grow even as share falls

  • The HBM market itself is expanding quickly, so even with share down from 64% to 50%, SK hynix's absolute HBM revenue has grown.
  • The issue is margin. If Samsung adds volume, SK hynix's pricing power could weaken in the next round of contracts.
  • So for SK hynix the metric to watch is HBM selling price, not share; for Samsung Electronics it is how fast its Nvidia volume ramps.

How big a threat is China's CXMT?

  • On Oct 12, CXMT said it will release server DDR5 RDIMMs by year-end using a 4F² structure that stacks cells more densely.
  • This is a threat to commodity server DRAM prices, not to HBM today. Rising commodity DRAM prices are a major pillar of this cycle's profits, which is why the market reacted sharply.
  • Production yields and Big Tech qualification are still unconfirmed. It is better read as a post-2027 pricing risk than a near-term negative.

Conclusion
Buying everything in one go today does not look like the favorable choice. There is no doubt about the three companies' profits, but what is driving prices right now is not profit; it is flows and the "peak debate." Approaching in stages through the earnings releases is the more reasonable path.
  • The good news is in the confirmed numbers. Samsung's Q3 operating profit of KRW 107.4 tn, SK hynix's first-half operating profit of KRW 98.1 tn and Micron's FY26 operating profit of $99.3 bn are results, not forecasts.
  • The bad news is concentrated in this moment. The KOSPI plunge, heavy foreign selling, the end of the buyback and the CXMT announcement all landed in the same week. A drop on a day like this often does not end in one day.
  • The three differ in character. Micron's chart and flows are the least damaged. Samsung Electronics has a firmer floor thanks to its dividend (about 3.8% in 2026E) and business diversification. SK hynix has the highest volatility (105% annualized), so it offers both the strongest bounce and the deepest further drop.
  • Remaining uncertainty. Whether memory prices hold in 2027 is the crux of every judgment, and it is an assumption no one can confirm yet.

Summary by Approach

If entering now

Commit only part of the planned total. Even as large caps, annual volatility of 90-105% means position size must be able to withstand daily moves of 5-10%. Decide in advance how to respond if the 200-day MA breaks.

If waiting

TSMC earnings, two interest-rate decisions and the SK hynix and Samsung results all arrive within three weeks. What waiting costs is part of the early rebound; what it gains is the companies' own answer to the "peak debate."

If already holding

The earnings logic is intact. However, the areas near KRW 1,400,000 for SK hynix, KRW 226,000 for Samsung Electronics and $942 for Micron are where the trend could change, so they are price levels at which to review position size.

10If Entering in Stages, at What Price Levels?

Indicators were calculated from four to five years of daily bars (about 1,100 trading days for Korea and about 1,250 for the US); weekly and monthly bars were built by aggregating the daily data.

How the Dante technique is reflected. "Dante" is the pen name of 주식단테, a Korean stock YouTuber known for chart-based methods built on long moving averages and "base candles" (large high-volume candles that mark institutional accumulation). This report marks both Dante's 112-, 224- and 448-day averages and the 122-, 244- and 444-day averages requested for the report, and this edition searches the daily bars directly for the signals Dante cites as evidence of "institutional accumulation," attaching a checklist for each stock. There are five criteria. ① Base candle (accumulation candle): a bullish candle with volume at least 2x the prior 20-day average and a body of 3% or more. ② Base candle open as support: whether later closes hold above that candle's open (Dante treats this open as the big players' average cost and stop-loss line). ③ Volume dry-up after the high-volume candle: how far the 10-day average volume after the base candle falls relative to the base candle. ④ Time correction below the 224-day MA: whether a "bowl pattern" second leg (sideways for four months or more) exists. ⑤ Suspected breakdown candle: a long bearish candle with at least 2x volume within 15% of the 52-week high. The ▲ markers and dotted lines on the chart show base candles within the last 150 trading days and their opens (orange = still holding, gray = already broken). These criteria were quantified from secondary sources that summarize the technique, not from Dante's original videos, so they may differ from Dante's own judgment.

What to Check When Price Reaches a Zone

ItemWhat a pullback looks likeWhat a breakdown looks like
VolumeArrives on volume below the 20-day average (SK hynix about 3.21 million shares, Samsung about 17.14 million, Micron about 25.55 million)Breaks the bottom of the zone on volume well above average
RSIDaily RSI falls below 30 and then rebounds back above 30Weekly RSI falls below 40, signaling a weakening trend
Candle shapeA long lower-shadow candle or a large bullish candle inside the zoneTwo or more consecutive closes below the zone
Foreign investorsForeign net selling of the two Korean stocks shrinks for two or more daysForeign net selling continues even as the index rebounds
MarketKOSPI holds 6,000 and the SOX holds its 60-day MA (about 12,000)Further index plunge. Individual support levels break easily during index crashes
Limitations of this chapter. This is general analysis summarizing where chart supports overlap; it is not investment advice tailored to any individual. The claim that price is highly likely to bounce when it touches a moving average is not a verified statistic. Price may bounce without reaching any of the three zones, or break through all of them. Memory stocks in particular have often seen technical supports fail around cycle turning points.
